worked.title: Q1 · Eigen-structure of a symmetric matrix (6 marks)

problem.text: A = [[4, 0, 2], [0, 3, 0], [2, 0, 1]]. (a) Eigenvalues and an eigenvector for each. [3M] (b) Orthogonal Q and diagonal Λ with A = QΛQᵀ. [1M] (c) rank(A) and a basis of Null(A). [1M] (d) Singular values and ‖A‖_F. [1M]

steps.label: (c)
steps.text: Two non-zero eigenvalues ⇒ rank 2; Null(A) = span{(1, 0, −2)}.

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text: Missing λ = 0 after factoring λ² − 5λ; not normalising the columns of Q.

worked.priorityWhy: Saurabh sir's Practice Paper: closest to the real exam

worked.title: Q2 · A system with two parameters (6 marks)

problem.text: x + 2y − z = 3, 2x + 5y + z = 8, x + 3y + λz = μ. (a) Echelon form. [2M] (b) Values of λ, μ for a unique solution, no solution, infinitely many. [2M] (c) In the infinite case: general solution and rank. [2M]

steps.label: (a)
steps.text: R2 − 2R1, R3 − R1, then R3 − R2 ⇒ last row [0 0 λ − 2 | μ − 5].

steps.label: (b)
steps.text: Unique: λ ≠ 2 (any μ). None: λ = 2, μ ≠ 5. Infinitely many: λ = 2, μ = 5.

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text: Forgetting μ doesn't matter when λ ≠ 2; a sign slip in x = 3 − 2y + z.

worked.answer: Unique if λ ≠ 2; none if λ = 2, μ ≠ 5; infinite if λ = 2, μ = 5: (−1, 2, 0) + t(7, −3, 1), rank 2.
worked.priorityWhy: Saurabh sir's Practice Paper: closest to the real exam

worked.title: Q3 · Inner product and Gram–Schmidt (6 marks)

problem.text: A = [[2, 1, 0], [1, 2, 0], [0, 0, 3]], ⟨x, y⟩ = xᵀAy, v₁ = (1, 0, 0), v₂ = (0, 1, 1). (a) Show it is an inner product. [2M] (b) Are v₁, v₂ orthogonal under the dot product? Under ⟨·,·⟩? [1M] (c) Gram–Schmidt under ⟨·,·⟩. [3M]

steps.label: (a)
steps.text: Symmetric; leading minors 2, 3, 9 > 0 ⇒ PD ⇒ inner product.

steps.label: (b)
steps.text: Dot product 0 ⇒ orthogonal. Av₁ = (2, 1, 0), ⟨v₂, v₁⟩ = 1 ≠ 0 ⇒ not orthogonal under A.

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text: Concluding orthogonal under A because the dot product is 0.

worked.answer: Inner product (minors 2, 3, 9); orthogonal under dot product, not under A; e₁ = (1/√2, 0, 0), e₂ = (−√2/6, √2/3, √2/3).
worked.priorityWhy: Saurabh sir's Practice Paper: closest to the real exam

worked.title: Q4 · Convex loss and momentum updates (6 marks)

problem.text: Fit ŷ = w₀ + w₁x to (1, 1), (2, 3), J = ½Σ(ŷᵢ − yᵢ)². (a) J, ∇J, Hessian; show J is convex. [2M] (b) Two momentum iterations from (0, 0), η = 0.05, β = 0.5, v₀ = 0. [3M] (c) The exact minimiser. [1M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Convexity from the Hessian, then the momentum recursion for two steps, then the exact minimiser. Marks: (a) 2, (b) 3, (c) 1.

steps.label: Plan of attack
steps.text: 1. Write J from the two residuals. 2. Differentiate each residual by the chain rule (don't expand the squares). 3. Hessian and leading minors. 4. Momentum table: gradient → velocity → weights. 5. Set ∇J = 0 for the exact answer.

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: Sourabh sir's symbols (η, β, v) are the same as the board's. Update: vₜ₊₁ = βvₜ − η∇J(wₜ), wₜ₊₁ = wₜ + vₜ₊₁, v₀ = 0.

steps.label: STEP 1 · (a) The data and the model
steps.text:
Two data points (x, y): (x₁, y₁) = (1, 1) and (x₂, y₂) = (2, 3).
Model: a straight line ŷ = w₀ + w₁x, where w₀ is the intercept and w₁ the slope. We want the w₀, w₁ that make ŷ close to y at both points.

steps.label: STEP 1 · (a) Predictions
steps.text:
Put each x into the model:
• At x₁ = 1: ŷ₁ = w₀ + w₁ × 1 = **w₀ + w₁**
• At x₂ = 2: ŷ₂ = w₀ + w₁ × 2 = **w₀ + 2w₁**

steps.label: STEP 1 · (a) Residuals
steps.text:
A residual is prediction minus true value, rᵢ = ŷᵢ − yᵢ:
• r₁ = ŷ₁ − y₁ = (w₀ + w₁) − 1 = **w₀ + w₁ − 1**
• r₂ = ŷ₂ − y₂ = (w₀ + 2w₁) − 3 = **w₀ + 2w₁ − 3**

steps.label: STEP 1 · (a) J
steps.text:
The question defines J = ½Σ(ŷᵢ − yᵢ)² = ½Σrᵢ²: half the sum of squared residuals (not a mean: there is no 1/n).
J = ½(r₁² + r₂²) = **½[(w₀ + w₁ − 1)² + (w₀ + 2w₁ − 3)²]**.
The ½ is there so that the 2 from differentiating a square cancels (STEP 2–3).

steps.label: STEP 1 · (a) J expanded (check)
steps.text:
(w₀ + w₁ − 1)² = w₀² + w₁² + 1 + 2w₀w₁ − 2w₀ − 2w₁
(w₀ + 2w₁ − 3)² = w₀² + 4w₁² + 9 + 4w₀w₁ − 6w₀ − 12w₁
Sum = 2w₀² + 5w₁² + 6w₀w₁ − 8w₀ − 14w₁ + 10
J = ½ × sum = **w₀² + 2.5w₁² + 3w₀w₁ − 4w₀ − 7w₁ + 5**.
Check: at the start (0, 0), J = 5 (= ½[1 + 9]). You don't need to expand in the exam; it only confirms the gradient in STEP 2–3.

steps.label: STEP 2 · (a) ∂J/∂w₀
steps.text:
∂J/∂w₀ = r₁ × ∂r₁/∂w₀ + r₂ × ∂r₂/∂w₀ = r₁ × 1 + r₂ × 1
= (w₀ + w₁ − 1) + (w₀ + 2w₁ − 3) = **2w₀ + 3w₁ − 4**.

steps.label: STEP 5 · (a) Convex
steps.text: Leading minors: D₁ = 2 > 0; D₂ = 2 × 5 − 3 × 3 = 10 − 9 = 1 > 0 ⇒ H is positive definite ⇒ **J is convex** (any local minimum is the global one).

steps.label: Quick check · finding a minimiser
steps.text:
**Always:** set the gradient to zero, **∇J = 0**, and solve the equations. Then confirm it is a minimum with the Hessian: H positive definite (leading minors > 0) ⇒ minimum.
Here: ∇J = (2w₀ + 3w₁ − 4, 3w₀ + 5w₁ − 7) = (0, 0) ⇒ (w₀, w₁) = (−1, 2), and H = [[2, 3], [3, 5]] is positive definite (STEP 5) ⇒ minimum.

steps.label: STEP 13 · (c) Exact minimiser
steps.text:
Set ∇J = 0: 2w₀ + 3w₁ = 4 … (i), 3w₀ + 5w₁ = 7 … (ii).
3 × (i): 6w₀ + 9w₁ = 12; 2 × (ii): 6w₀ + 10w₁ = 14. Subtract: w₁ = 2.
Put into (i): 2w₀ + 6 = 4 ⇒ w₀ = −1.

steps.label: STEP 14 · (c) Check
steps.text: ŷ = −1 + 2x gives ŷ(1) = 1 and ŷ(2) = 3: both points exactly, so J = 0, the minimum.

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• Using +η∇J in the velocity.
• Forgetting βv₁ in step 2.
• Expanding the squares and making an algebra slip: differentiate the residuals instead.

worked.title: Q5 · PCA: scores and explained variance (6 marks)

problem.text: Points (2, 0), (0, 2), (3, 3), (−1, −1); S = (1/N)X_cᵀX_c. (a) Mean and X_c. [1M] (b) S. [1M] (c) Eigenvalues and unit eigenvectors. [2M] (d) First PC, the scores zₙ, fraction of variance. [2M]

steps.label: (d)
steps.text: PC1 = q₁; scores 0, 0, 2√2, −2√2; explained 4/5 = 80%.

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text: Building S from un-centred data; mixing 1/N and 1/(N − 1); a non-unit eigenvector.

worked.answer: λ = 4, 1; PC1 (1, 1)/√2; scores 0, 0, 2√2, −2√2; 80% of the variance.

worked.title: Q6 · Hard-margin SVM: verify and use (5 marks)

problem.text: (2, 2)+, (4, 3)+, (0, 0)−, (−1, 0)−; solver gives w = (½, ½), b = −1. (a) Primal. (b) Check constraints, support vectors, α's. (c) Margin. (d) Classify (3, 0) and (1, 0.5).

steps.label: Solution
steps.text: Support vectors (2, 2) and (0, 0); α = (¼, 0, ¼, 0); margin √2; (3, 0) → +1, (1, 0.5) → −1. Every step: [Lecture 14, Hard margin tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch14/f-hard/2).
